incidents.title: Caller hears silence after a carrier move
incidents.summary: The 200 OK is fine. The address in c= is not.
incidents.epilogue: Signaling health is not media health.

steps.prompt: The ladder completes. What do you open next?
steps.log:
SIP/2.0 200 OK
CSeq: 1 INVITE
Content-Type: application/sdp
c=IN IP4 10.1.2.3
m=audio 19642 RTP/AVP 0
choices: The c= line and whether 10.1.2.3 is reachable
steps.why: 10.1.2.3 is not a public address. The phone will send RTP there and get nothing back.

steps.prompt: TLS is not in use on this hop. What else rewrites private addresses into SDP?
steps.log:
INVITE left the PBX with c=IN IP4 203.0.113.20
The carrier captured c=IN IP4 10.1.2.3
choices: A SIP ALG on the path
steps.why: ALGs rewrite SDP and then fail when the rewritten address is useless.

steps.prompt: The fastest safe change is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Anchor media on the SBC you control and disable the ALG
Switch the codec to G.722 only
steps.why: Media anchoring gives the carrier a public address you own. The ALG has to go. Give the far end an address that routes, and stop the middlebox from editing SDP.

incidents.title: Every Webex call dies with 488
incidents.summary: The trunk is up. The offer has no codec the answerer will take.

steps.prompt: Where does 488 point?
steps.log:
SIP/2.0 488 Not Acceptable Here
CSeq: 1 INVITE
Warning: 304 example.com "Media type not available"
choices: This endpoint rejected the SDP offer
steps.why: 488 is about this UA’s media, not about routing.

steps.prompt: The offer lists only G.729. The peer’s answer template lists PCMU and telephone-event. What is the overlap?
steps.log:
m=audio 49170 RTP/AVP 18
a=rtpmap:18 G729/8000
choices: The call should fall back inside RTP
steps.why: PT 18 is G.729 in the static table. It was not offered by the peer.

steps.prompt: What do you change?
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Add a shared codec, usually PCMU, on the SBC offer
steps.why: Port 0 would reject the stream on purpose. You need a shared encoding name. Offer a codec the peer actually answers.

incidents.title: Teams marks the SBC inactive
incidents.summary: OPTIONS never completes. The certificate name and the Contact FQDN disagree.

steps.prompt: The admin center says inactive. What must succeed first?
steps.log:
SBC TLS connect to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com:5061
Contact: <sip:203.0.113.20:5061;transport=tls>
choices: OPTIONS over TLS with 200 OK, and a Contact FQDN
steps.why: Direct Routing health is OPTIONS, and an IP in Contact is refused.

steps.prompt: The certificate SAN is sbc1.example.com. The Contact host is 203.0.113.20. Microsoft’s rule is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: The FQDN in Contact must match the certificate name
steps.why: IP hosts are rejected with 403. The name has to be the one in the certificate.

steps.prompt: TLS version on the SBC is 1.0. The troubleshooting article says
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
steps.why: The documented requirement is TLS 1.2 or higher. Present the FQDN, a public certificate, and TLS 1.2, then confirm OPTIONS both ways.

incidents.title: International minutes at 02:00
incidents.summary: A diagnostic, not a recipe. The source address was never on the trust list.

steps.prompt: The CDR export shows 200 calls to premium international destinations from one UDP source. First control to check?
steps.log:
show ip address trusted list
Source 198.51.100.250 is not listed
INVITE sip:90114415551212@203.0.113.20
choices: Whether that source is allowed to place VoIP calls
steps.why: IOS voice trusted-IP authentication is the documented toll-fraud control.

steps.prompt: A dial-peer matches destination-pattern 9T and points at the carrier. The risk is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Any caller who can reach the SBC can place outbound calls that match 9T
steps.why: A wide pattern plus an open source list is the expensive combination.

steps.prompt: The defensive change is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Trust only known peers and narrow outbound patterns
Publish the SBC on 0.0.0.0/0 and hope
steps.why: Add the real peers to the trusted list. Do not open the list to every address. Restrict who may send INVITEs, then restrict what they may dial.

incidents.title: Calls drop at the same age
incidents.summary: Both sides want a refresh. They never agreed the interval.

steps.prompt: The second response is
steps.log:
SIP/2.0 422 Session Interval Too Small
Min-SE: 1800
CSeq: 1 INVITE
choices: The peer’s minimum session interval is higher than the offer
steps.why: 422 and Min-SE are session timers.

steps.prompt: Who sends the refresh?
steps.log: Session-Expires: 1800;refresher=uac
choices: The refresher parameter says which side
steps.why: refresher is uac or uas.

steps.prompt: A working retry uses
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
steps.why: Raise the offered interval to the peer’s minimum and try again. Honor Min-SE. Do not loop 422 with the same value.

incidents.title: CUCM inserts an MTP and audio sounds like a tunnel
incidents.summary: The INVITE left without SDP. Something on the trunk demanded an MTP.

steps.prompt: This INVITE is
steps.log:
INVITE sip:+15551212@198.51.100.30 SIP/2.0
Content-Length: 0
steps.why: No SDP in the INVITE means the offer is not here.

steps.prompt: CUCM may add an MTP when the trunk requires one. The lab’s advice is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Read the CUCM trunk guide for that version before assuming the checkbox
steps.why: MTP required is real, and the exact UI belongs to the version’s admin guide.

steps.prompt: If the carrier needs early offer, the CUBE knob documented for that is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: voice-class sip early-offer forced on the outbound dial-peer
codec g729 only with no offer
steps.why: early-offer forced is the CUBE mechanism. Confirm it in the configuration guide. Decide which hop is allowed to delay the offer, and force early offer only where the peer requires it.

incidents.title: 483 after a routing loop
incidents.summary: Two proxies keep sending the request to each other.

steps.prompt: The response is 483 Too Many Hops. The header that ran out is
steps.log:
SIP/2.0 483 Too Many Hops
CSeq: 1 INVITE
steps.why: Each hop decrements Max-Forwards. Zero becomes 483.

steps.prompt: The Record-Route set shows the same two proxies alternating. That means
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: A routing loop, not a codec problem
steps.why: Look at Route and the request URI, not the m-line.

steps.prompt: The fix is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Correct the route so the request leaves the loop
Raise Max-Forwards to 1000 and keep the loop
steps.why: A higher Max-Forwards only delays the failure. Break the loop in the dial plan or Route set.

steps.prompt: The PBX sent Diversion. The SBC’s outbound INVITE has no Diversion and no History-Info. Unity keys the greeting from
steps.log:
INVITE sip:voicemail@198.51.100.40 SIP/2.0
To: <sip:+15551212@example.com>
(no Diversion, no History-Info)
choices: The original called number, which is now missing
steps.why: Diversion is widely used and is not the standards-track history mechanism. History-Info is.

steps.prompt: A CUBE teaching rule that deletes every Diversion looks like
steps.log: request INVITE sip-header Diversion remove
choices: That rule explains the missing header
That rule is an RTP command
steps.why: remove drops the header on the way out.

steps.prompt: The interop choice is
steps.log: (No extra packet. Decide from the prompt and the last trace.)
choices: Pass Diversion or map it to History-Info on purpose
steps.why: Decide the history header the voicemail system documents, and keep that one. Restore the header the voicemail integration guide names.
